why: Who owns a `send-message` effect once a turn hands it back. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END: every `interactionSelect` completion left two of them in the browser console as `[DEBUG] wireEffectToFriendly: unmapped effect "send-message" dropped — unverified wasm-boundary conversion`, which read like lost work. It was not: `route_app_frame` (`⚛️reactor/🔄️turn/🦀️.rs`) wraps EVERY non-`UiPatch` `AppFrame` reply in `Effect::SendMessage{Shell{instance}}`, the reserved-tool-job completion turn parks them in `pendingTurnEffects`, and `invocationFromFrames` already applies them through `leftoverShellInvocationFrames` (the history patch the console logs one line later) before handing the SAME list to the friendly mapping. A shell or backbone send-message is transport with an owner; anything else has no host route at all and must stay loud.

cases.why: The `interactionSelect` shape: an AppFrame reply addressed at the calling instance. `shellFrameBytes` hands back its payload and the friendly mapping must stay silent.
`shellFrameBytes` declines a frame addressed elsewhere, but it is still transport owned by that other instance's own drain — never a friendly effect this instance should act on, and never a warning.
`routeHostEffects` already pushed this out the bound document port before the friendly mapping ran.
The real hole the old blanket drop was hiding: no consumer anywhere routes a topic-addressed message, so this one MUST stay loud.
A target-less send-message is malformed, not transport.
The default arm keeps its meaning: an effect kind with no case at all is still an honest, loud drop.

The wgpu door had NO case for this effect at all, so a binary export vanished into the loud default drop; and where a door did map it, the WIT `option<string>` arrives as `{tag:"some"}` and a flat read lost it. Both halves are pinned here. The bytes this `data` must become are `🎠️kernel/🧫️fixtures/⬇️media-export-encoding/🔣️.json`'s law.
jco's direct binding hands the same field over bare — the other real shape of one `option<string>`.
A textual export declares no encoding; a `none` variant and an absent field mean the same thing and must not become the string "none".

The exact `interactionHover` reserved tool job recorded on 6118 (job 909, 174 B). Before this row the wgpu bridge had NO `spawn-job` case: this effect hit the default arm as `unmapped effect "spawn-job" dropped`, twice per gesture, and the hover was published perfectly and applied never.

cases.why: `cancel-job` is the other half of the same door and was dropped by the same missing case.
An unrecognised `job-placement` is refused, never defaulted: guessing `inline` would run a pooled job inside the spawning instance's own turn budget.
The guest's `RequestRegistry` never issues 0 — the same bound `respond`/`invoke-extension` put on `req`.
A job with no kind names no registered factory; admitting it would start a job nothing can step.
Control row — the new case must not shadow a real friendly projection.

u64FieldsWhy: A WIT `u64` reaches the decoder as a jco `bigint`, which JSON cannot carry. The fixture states these fields as decimal TEXT and every reader rehydrates them to `BigInt` before driving the decoder — narrowing one to a `number` would silently mis-resolve a long-lived actor's parked futures.
bytesFieldsWhy: A `pack`/`list<u8>` field is stated as `{"base64": "…"}` so a recorded payload stays byte-exact and readable; readers decode it to a `Uint8Array` before driving the decoder.
